Affiliation:: University of Oklahoma, Data Science and Analytics Institute, Data Institute for Societal Challenges
Techniques Used: Long Short Term Memory Recurrent Neural Network (LSTM-RNN)
Data & Platforms: German Portal for Medical Research Data (FDPG)
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Hypothesis-Driven Data Integration: This researcher integrates multiple communication-based NLP dimensions with a base LLM to holistically evaluate trustworthiness in news articles, as seen in the development of TRUExT, which uses a compiled training dataset and fine-tunes the RoBERTa model to achieve high correlation coefficients and low MSE losses.

Radiomic Imaging Analysis: This researcher uses radiomic imaging markers to predict long-term functional risk in ischemic stroke survivors, demonstrating the potential of composite tools using Recursive Feature Elimination and Support Vector Machine on raw features, and Logistic Regression on transformed features.

Deep Learning for Material Properties: This researcher employs deep learning features to predict rock elastic properties for unconventional shales using texture and pore aspect ratios acquired from BSE-SEM images, showing that texture is sufficient to capture mineralogy and the juxtaposition of various minerals.

Data-Driven Visualization: This researcher emphasizes the importance of data visualization in preparing for and responding to future pandemics, identifying key challenges and proposing action points to address them, including developing a readiness data platform and integrating emerging technologies.
Summary Description: David Ebert is a researcher with expertise in data science, machine learning, and natural language processing. His work focuses on developing tools and methods for evaluating trustworthiness in news articles, predicting long-term functional outcomes in ischemic stroke survivors, and analyzing material properties for unconventional shales. He also explores the role of data visualization in pandemic response and public health. His research combines machine learning, deep learning, and radiomic imaging to address complex problems in data science and medical research.
